newsitem.title: CHINA: China to treat Taiwan JV bank as foreigner.
newsitem.headline: China to treat Taiwan JV bank as foreigner.

text.p: The first joint venture bank between China and Taiwan business interests will be treated as a foreign bank if it applies to do local currency yuan business, officials said on Thursday.

An official with the joint venture's Chinese partner, the Shanghai Pudong Development Bank, said the joint venture bank would apply to the central bank for the yuan business and wait for the approval as foreign banks are doing.
"Banks from Hong Kong need approval if they want to handle yuan business, let alone a joint venture," he said.
But the official added that the central bank had said banks from Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan would have some advantages in applying for domestic yuan business.
He declined to say what those advantages were.
The official China Daily reported on Sunday the plan to set up the China-Taiwan joint venture bank with a registered capital of $100 million had been approved in principle by the central bank.
The partners in the venture are the state-owned Pudong Development Bank and a group of overseas-registered Taiwan businesses.

The Pudong Development Bank official declined to name the Taiwan partners, adding that the joint venture bank was still waiting for a licence that would specify its formal name, opening date and capital structure.
Media reports in Taiwan have said it will be called China First Bank.
The official Shanghai-based Business News reported on Thursday that Taiwan-invested firms would be the bank's main clients followed by firms with investment from overseas Chinese.
